result.proposed_fix: In untrusted.py, replace the enumerated _DOTCH/_DOT with a category-based separator. Inside a whitespace-separated token (on the normalised text and the skeleton), any run of characters whose Unicode category is P* or S* (Sk included) counts as a dot, except a single word-internal '-', "'" or '\u2019', and '/'. So do 'dot'/'d0t' in any wrapper or spacing ('_dot_', '-dot-', '{dot}', ' d0t '), and an optional space on either side of a dot-like mark. The match counts when the right-hand label is 2-63 letters or an ACE label. Keep the existing precision-only exceptions (a full stop, comma or colon plus space plus capitalised word; 'rose.The'; the CJK '。' break; abbreviations). Also run has_link_or_contact on the whole unsplit source paragraph and on the joined answer text, and quote or drop any sentence next to a LINK_OR_CONTACT hit, so splitter-split links ('portal . Com') cannot survive in halves. Replace string-list regressions with generated ones: every code point in categories Po/Pd/Ps/Pe/Sk/Sm placed between 'refunds-portal' and 'com' (and doubled), through has_link_or_contact, mask_links, verify, extractive, build_surface and require_valid, with tests embedded in the test file.
result.root_cause: The link detector in uri_web/untrusted.py is still a list of known separator shapes, not a rule. _BARE (untrusted.py:78) matches a bare domain only when the labels are joined by _DOT (untrusted.py:76), and _DOT accepts only the 14 characters in _DOTCH (untrusted.py:75), certain bracket pairs and a spaced 'dot'. Any other separator a reader would take as a dot makes has_link_or_contact return False. Probes at HEAD 806dcd12 found: 'refunds..com/claim', 'refunds…com', U+060C, U+0964, U+0589, U+06D4, U+2E31, U+0701, U+16EB, U+1362, U+0F0B, U+A789, U+02D9, ',', ':', ' d0t ', '_dot_', '-dot-', 'refunds-portal.c om'. Each of these is kept unquoted by verify() (synthesize.py:238), picked by extractive() (synthesize.py:318), shown by build_surface via clean/mask_links (surface.py:38) and accepted by require_valid. The literal R5-01 strings ('_refunds-portal.com_' and the others) are fixed at HEAD by 29771992's (?<![^\W_])...(?![^\W_]) lookarounds. What recurs is the class (R1-01/R5-01/R6-01): a link next to a separator the list does not cover. A second, smaller path: the sentence splitter (evaluate.py:38 _SENT) splits 'refunds-portal . Com' / 'refunds-portal. Com/claim' into two sentences that are each link-free, and verify/extractive keep the halves.
result.why_earlier_repairs_failed: Each repair added the shapes the reviewer had just reported and wrote regression tests for those exact strings. ca622bc0 added [.]/(.)/[dot]. f3700643 added U+3002/U+FF0E/U+FF61. 462be42c added spaced bracket defangs. f5a5b8ec added the ACE 'xn--' top-level label. 29771992 (the R5-01 repair, not in the listed repairs) changed only the '_'/'-' lookarounds. 806dcd12 (D13, 'mask any dot-joined word') turned the owner's rule into another fixed set, _DOTCH, which leaves out most Unicode full stops and dot-like marks (Po/Sk), repeated dots and the ellipsis, ASCII ',' and ':', and spelled forms like 'd0t', '_dot_' and '-dot-'. The tests (e.g. tests/web/test_w1_closure_r5_review_regressions.py:23 WRAPPED) list fixed strings, so the next unlisted separator always passes. None of the repairs looked at the splitter running before the per-sentence check.
